item.title: Kenya: Mysterious illness kills more than a dozen elephants
item.description: In Kenya, since the end of June, at least 19 elephants, mostly females or young animals, have died after displaying the same symptoms, notably partial paralysis preventing them from standing. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Worries grow over mysterious illness killing Kenyan elephants
item.description: Worries over the death of elephants are mounting in southern Kenya, where at least 19 animals have died since June from an unexplained condition. With symptoms including partial paralysis, conservationists and communities are demanding urgent investigations into what is killing the elephants. Fuente: Africanews.
item.dc:creator: editorial@africanews.com (Dominic Wabwireh)

item.title: Congo: Ebola cases are rising at record pace
item.description: The Ebola virus is spreading rapidly in the DRC. In Kinshasa, a city of millions, fears of a serious health crisis are growing. Hospitals are scrambling to prepare for emergencies as best as they can. Fuente: Deutsche Welle - World.

item.title: El último aliento de un paciente en una sala de ébola del Congo
item.description: La línea que separa la vida de la muerte es muy delgada en una clínica médica de Rwampara, en el epicentro de la epidemia que asola la República Democrática del Congo. Fuente: Clarín - Mundo.
item.dc:creator: Clarin.com - Home

item.title: Una ciudad se moviliza contra una persistente amenaza para la salud: los mosquitos
item.description: La ciudad de Belém, en el norte de Brasil, se vio desbordada por un brote de dengue hace dos años. Un esfuerzo municipal a gran escala ha logrado reducir el número de casos y podría servir de ejemplo. Fuente: Clarín - Mundo.
item.dc:creator: Clarin.com - Home

item.title: An attack on healthcare every six hours, and no one held to account
item.description: Across the world, healthcare has suffered more than 10,000 attacks in the past eight years, including during the brutal conflict in Ukraine and efforts to contain the current Ebola outbreak spreading rapidly in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). Fuente: UN News.

item.title: Miles ahead: China team boosts atom entanglement distance record fourfold
item.description: Chinese scientists have achieved the quantum entanglement of cold atoms across a record-breaking 420km (260 miles), a breakthrough they say lays the groundwork for intercity quantum networks. According to a paper published by the peer-reviewed journal Physical Review Letters on August 11, the distance was more than four times previous demonstrations and exceeded the threshold at which direct transmission encounters fundamental physical limits. “Our experiment provides a test bed for studying... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: Dannie Peng

item.title: Hong Kong teen’s will to fight illness ‘incredibly low’ after near-death scares
item.description: A teenager who fears dying young has narrowly escaped death twice this year after contracting influenza and respiratory virus infection, enduring what he described as his “most emotionally devastating breakdown”. Chen Tsz-kin, 17, was diagnosed with the incurable muscle-wasting disease at the age of 18 months and was told that people with the condition had an average life expectancy of 18. In a Facebook post on Thursday, he revealed that he had experienced two near-death episodes this year,... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: Cannix Yau

item.title: DR Congo's fastest-growing ebola outbreak spreads to sixth province
item.description: Man dies in Bas-Uele after travelling from Haut-Uele, as head of WHO says outbreak on track to be deadliest ever The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has spread to a sixth province, officials have said, a day after the head of the World Health Organization said the outbreak was on track to surpass the deadliest in history, which killed at least 11,000 people more than a decade ago. The current outbreak has killed more than 2,100 people out of more than 4,500 cases, according to the latest government figures released on Tuesday. item.title: 6088 reproducciones · 77 reacciones | Vaccines protect people at every stage of life: from a child’s first days through adulthood and beyond. In early childhood, immune systems are still developing, leaving young children more vulnerable to serious illness. That’s why most routine vaccines are given in the first two years of life, offering protection when it matters most. As children grow into their teenage years, booster doses help keep that protection strong and respond to new and emerging health risks. During pregnancy, vaccination plays a crucial role in protecting both parent and baby. Recommended vaccines help pass protective antibodies to babies before birth, giving them a safer start in life. In adulthood and older age, the immune system naturally becomes less robust. Vaccines help reduce the risk of severe illness and hospitalization, helping people stay healthy and live longer. Vaccination is about care, prevention and giving every generation the chance to learn, grow and thrive. #VaccinesWork | World Health Organization (WHO)

item.title: EE. UU.: desgaste de militares del UUSS Abraham Lincoln estaría afectando su salud mental
item.description: La situación a bordo del portaaviones USS Abraham Lincoln ha encendido las alarmas entre familiares de miembros de la tripulación y legisladores estadounidenses, ante denuncias de escasez de suministros, problemas con el agua y la infraestructura del buque y, especialmente, un deterioro de la salud mental de quienes llevan meses en alta mar. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Young Talent Time host Johnny Young dies
item.description: Young Talent Time host Johnny Young has died aged 79 following a brief battle with pancreatic cancer. Fuente: ABC News Australia.
item.dc:creator: Rudi Maxwell, Callum Liddelow, and Stephanie Chalkley-Rhoden

item.title: ¿Qué está pasando en el USS Abraham Lincoln? La alarma por las condiciones de sus 5.000 tripulantes
item.description: Tras más de 250 días de despliegue, familiares y legisladores estadounidenses denuncian escasez de suministros, problemas sanitarios y una creciente crisis de salud mental entre los 5.000 tripulantes del USS Lincoln. El Pentágono niega las acusaciones, pero ya otro portaaviones se dirige a Medio Oriente para reemplazarlo. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: France 24

item.title: Mutation hotspots help 'friendly' viruses outmaneuver the bacteria in your gut
item.description: Every 15 minutes, someone in the U.S. dies from a drug-resistant superbug. A few decades from now, antibiotic-resistant bacterial infections threaten to become the leading cause of death worldwide, outpacing cancer. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How to fine-tune molecular structures within vaccines to improve immune responses
item.description: A vaccine's molecular structure plays a key role in determining how the immune system responds and prepares to protect the body from future exposure to a specific pathogen. To develop a vaccine that offers long-term protection from HIV, it's essential to promote a long-lasting immune response in which immune cells and antibodies prepared to combat the virus persist within the body. This has inspired scientists to find ways to alter vaccine structure to increase the duration and persistence of the immune response. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Trump’s FDA insists explosive diarrhea outbreak parasite is removed from food supply - but cases keep growing
item.description: There are now nearly 25,000 cases of cyclosporiasis in dozens of states nationwide Fuente: The Independent - World.

item.title: Crisis a bordo de un portaaviones de EE.UU.: marineros agotados, problemas de salud mental y denuncias de intentos de suicidio
item.description: El USS Abraham Lincoln lleva nueve meses en alta mar y sus 5000 tripulantes cumplen jornadas de hasta 16 horas; familiares denuncian escasez de alimentos y productos básicos y un grave deterioro psicológico Fuente: La Nación - El Mundo.

item.title: Replacement aircraft carrier heading to Middle East after complaints about conditions on USS Lincoln
item.description: Family members say sailors on the USS Abraham Lincoln have faced food shortages, long stretches at sea and deteriorating mental health Fuente: The Independent - World.
item.dc:creator: Josh Marcus

item.title: A City Mobilizes Against a Stubborn Health Threat: Mosquitoes
item.description: The city of Belém in northern Brazil was overwhelmed by an outbreak of dengue two years ago. An all-out municipal effort has reduced cases and may offer lessons to American cities. Fuente: The New York Times - World.
item.dc:creator: Apoorva Mandavilli and Alessandro Falco

item.title: Fastest-growing Ebola outbreak spreads to previously unaffected area
item.description: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak has spread to a sixth province after a death was recorded in the previously unaffected Bas-Uele province. Fuente: Sky News - World.

item.title: Ebola tracing improves in DR Congo – but the virus is still winning the race
item.description: Health authorities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) are tracking a growing share of people exposed to Ebola, but the epidemic in the country's restive east continues to outpace their ability to find and isolate the sick, the World Health Organization (WHO) has warned. Fuente: UN News.

item.title: DRC: World Health Organisation Chief sounds alarm on ebola outbreak
item.description: Having returned from a trip to the Democratic Republic of Congo, the world health organisaiton chief is sounding the alarm on the ebola outbreak. Fuente: Africanews.

item.title: Congo’s Ebola outbreak on track to surpass deadliest in history, WHO chief says
item.description: “At its current pace, it’s on track to eclipse the West African Ebola outbreak of 2014 to 2016,” WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus told reporters on Wednesday. Fuente: Euronews.

item.title: Toddler's tragic death from brain-destroying amoeba offers lessons for doctors
item.description: Boy's unusual symptoms could help identify the next case sooner. Fuente: Ars Technica.
item.dc:creator: Beth Mole

item.title: India, Southern African customs bloc revive trade pact talks
item.description: The move revives talks between India and SACU, comprising South Africa, Botswana, Namibia, Lesotho and Eswatini, after five rounds ‌of negotiations between 2002 and 2010 ended without a deal Fuente: The Hindu - International.

item.title: Ebola outbreak takes heavy toll on Bunia's economy and public health
item.description: Health officials say misinformation and delayed treatment continue to fuel the outbreak. Fuente: Africanews.
item.dc:creator: editorial@africanews.com

item.title: Cholera spreads across borders in West and Central Africa
item.description: Cholera is spreading rapidly across West and Central Africa, with active outbreaks now in six countries and millions of children at growing risk, UN children’s agency UNICEF has said. Fuente: UN News.

item.title: Ebola deaths top 2,000 as scientists race to develop vaccine
item.description: Local officials in the DR Congo (DRC) reported on Tuesday that deaths from the Ebola virus disease have surpassed 2,000, with half of that number in the last 20 days. Fuente: UN News.

item.title: DR Congo: Ebola is killing people before they ever reach a doctor
item.description: More than 1,900 people have died in the Democratic Republic of the Congo's Ebola outbreak – and most of them never made it to a treatment centre. Between 60 and 70 per cent of deaths are happening in communities far from care, a gap that is now central to the World Health Organization's response. Fuente: UN News.
